props.description: Semantic color variant.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label surfaced via aria-label.

props.name: isPulsing
props.description: Enables a pulse animation; respects prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.

props.name: tooltip
props.description: Tooltip text shown on hover to explain the status meaning.

props.name: icon
props.description: Optional icon rendered centered inside the dot, painted in currentColor (the variant's ink). Gives the status a non-color mark, so use a different icon per status. Booleans and empty strings are ignored, so `cond && <Icon />` is safe. Same contract as AvatarStatusDot.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

components.name: Step
components.description: Individual step within a Stepper. Renders a progress-bar segment, an indicator, and a label with optional description. Progress (completed/active/not-started) is derived from the parent Stepper's activeStep and this step's step index.

props.name: step
props.description: Zero-based index of this step. Used to derive progress (completed/active/not-started) relative to the parent activeStep.

props.name: label
props.description: Step label text. Kept to a single line and ellipsized when the step is narrower than the label, so a row of horizontal steps stays the same height and the track under them stays straight. The full string is still read out as part of the step, so a truncated label costs nothing in the accessible name — but short labels survive narrow layouts better.

props.name: description
props.description: Optional description shown below the label for additional context.

props.name: children
props.description: Content rendered below the label and description. Useful in vertical steppers for form fields or detailed step content. In a compact horizontal Stepper, the content remains mounted to preserve local state while it is hidden with the expanded step details.

props.name: status
props.description: Semantic color for the step. Controls color only and maps to the global Astryx semantic tokens. Leave unset for the progress-derived default coloring.

props.name: indicator
props.description: What to show as the step indicator. 'auto' shows a number until completed then a check, 'number' always shows a numbered badge, 'none' hides it, or pass any ReactNode (e.g. an Icon) for a fully custom indicator.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables interaction and dims the step indicator and label.

props.name: isOptional
props.description: Marks the step as optional, appending an "Optional" affordance after the label.

props.name: endContent
props.description: Trailing content rendered at the end of the label row.

props.name: density
props.description: Controls vertical padding of the step. Falls back to the stepper-level density when unset.

components.name: Stepper
components.description: Steppers display progress through a sequence of logical and numbered steps. Use them for multi-step workflows like forms, onboarding flows, or checkout processes where users need to see their position and the steps ahead. Rendered as an ordered list (not a navigation landmark).

components.name: Switch
components.description: A toggle control for on/off states that take effect immediately. Supports labels, descriptions, loading states, and validation. Use it for settings or preferences that apply instantly. For changes requiring a form submission, use a checkbox instead. Under a finger it moves like the iOS switch on every touch screen: a press lifts the thumb, a drag across flips it, lifting the finger commits, and a tap toggles through the browser’s click. The thumb keeps its circle and size on every device, and under a coarse pointer the invisible hit area grows toward 44 × 44 px, stopping halfway to any neighbouring control so a tap goes to the nearer one. With reduced motion on, a change cross-fades on a touch screen and is immediate with a mouse.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the underlying <input> element.

props.name: label
props.description: Label text for the switch (always rendered for accessibility).

props.name: value
props.description: Whether the switch is on or off.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Callback fired when the switch state changes.

props.name: changeAction
props.description: Async action fired after onChange. Triggers optimistic UI and shows a loading spinner until the promise resolves.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Whether the switch is in a loading state, showing a spinner inside the thumb.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Visually hides the label while keeping it accessible to screen readers.

props.name: description
props.description: Description text displayed below the label.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether the switch is disabled.

props.name: size
props.description: Size variant controlling track and thumb dimensions. sm (32x20px) matches sm checkbox/radio vertical rhythm; md (40x24px, default) matches md checkbox/radio vertical rhythm.

props.name: htmlName
props.description: The HTML name attribute for the underlying checkbox input, useful for form submissions (submits "on" when the switch is on).

props.name: disabledMessage
props.description: Explains why the switch is disabled. With isDisabled, shows a tooltip on hover/keyboard focus and keeps the switch focusable via aria-disabled (toggling stays blocked). Use this instead of wrapping a disabled Switch in Tooltip. Disabled controls swallow the hover events an external Tooltip needs.

props.name: isOptional
props.description: Whether the field is optional. Mutually exclusive with isRequired.

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Whether the switch is required. Mutually exclusive with isOptional.

props.name: status
props.description: Status indicator with type and message. Displays a colored message box below the switch and sets aria-invalid when type is "error".

props.name: onFocus
props.description: Callback fired when the switch receives focus.

props.name: onBlur
props.description: Callback fired when the switch loses focus.

props.name: labelIcon
props.description: Icon displayed before the label text. See `astryx docs icons` for valid semantic names.

props.name: labelTooltip
props.description: Tooltip text shown in an info icon at the end of the label.

props.name: labelPosition
props.description: Which side of the switch the label appears on. "start" places the label before the switch.

props.name: labelSpacing
props.description: Spacing behavior between label and switch. "hug" places them next to each other; "spread" pushes them to opposite ends of the container (full width).

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the field (number = pixels, string used as-is, e.g. "100%"). Sizes the whole field (label, control, and status) so they stay aligned.

components.name: SyntaxTheme
components.description: Applies syntax highlighting colors to CodeBlock and any code component in the subtree. By default, code components use the theme-level syntax colors (set via defineTheme({ syntax: ... })), which derive from the palette (--color-text-accent for keywords, --color-text-green for strings, etc.). SyntaxTheme lets you override those per-region. The system uses 14 semantic tokens (keyword, string, comment, number, function, type, variable, operator, constant, tag, attribute, property, punctuation, background) validated against 11 community themes. Custom themes are created with defineSyntaxTheme() and can use [light, dark] tuples for automatic color-scheme adaptation. Built-in presets: oneDarkPro, dracula, monokai, nord, tokyoNight, catppuccinMocha, githubLight, githubDark, solarizedLight, oneLight (import from @astryxdesign/core/theme/syntax).

props.name: theme
props.description: Syntax highlighting theme: a preset from @astryxdesign/core/theme/syntax or a custom theme created with defineSyntaxTheme().

props.name: children
props.description: Content subtree. All CodeBlock components within will use this syntax theme.

components.name: Tab
components.description: Individual tab item that renders as a button or an anchor link, with selected-state styling and optional icons.

props.name: value
props.description: Unique value for this tab, matched against TabListContext.value.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for this tab. Used as visible text by default, or as aria-label when isLabelHidden is true.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Whether the label is visually hidden. When true, only the icon and endContent are displayed, and label is used as aria-label for accessibility.

props.name: href
props.description: URL to navigate to; when provided, the tab renders as an anchor element. Ignored in a TabList given an explicit role="tablist".

props.name: panelId
props.description: Id of the panel this tab controls, wired up as aria-controls where the TabList speaks the tabs pattern. Put the same id on the panel element. No effect under the navigation pattern, and a development warning says so.

props.name: as
props.description: Custom component to render instead of <a> for link tabs. Overrides the LinkProvider default. Only applies when href is provided.

props.name: icon
props.description: Icon element shown when the tab is not selected.

props.name: selectedIcon
props.description: Icon element shown when the tab is selected; falls back to icon if not provided.

props.name: endContent
props.description: Content rendered after the label, such as a badge count or status dot.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

components.name: Table
components.description: Styled, data-driven table with density, dividers, hover highlight, striped rows, and named plugin support. T must extend Record<string, unknown>.

props.name: data
props.description: Array of data items to render as rows. T must extend Record<string, unknown> (use `interface MyRow extends Record<string, unknown>` for custom types).

props.name: columns
props.description: Column definitions: each column has {key, header, width?, align?, renderCell?}. The `header` field sets the column heading text. If omitted, columns are auto-generated from data object keys. The `width` field is typed as `ColumnWidth` (not a number); use `proportional(n)` or `pixel(n)` helpers imported from `@astryxdesign/core/Table`. Omitting `width` keeps an equal flexible share with a compact 60px readability floor. To give one column a different floor, set `width: proportional(1, {minWidth: 80})`; its `minWidth` replaces the 60px floor for that column. Example: `width: pixel(120)` for 120px fixed, `width: proportional(1)` for a flexible column with a 120px default minimum.

props.name: idKey
props.description: Row key for React reconciliation. Pass a property name string or a function. Falls back to row index if omitted.

props.name: density
props.description: Row density controlling cell padding and font size.

props.name: dividers
props.description: Divider style rendered between cells.

props.name: isStriped
props.description: Applies a background wash to even-numbered rows.

props.name: hasHover
props.description: Applies a hover highlight background to rows on pointer devices.

props.name: verticalAlign
props.description: Vertical alignment for body row cells. Controls `vertical-align` on the `<td>` elements.

props.name: textOverflow
props.description: How body cell text behaves when it exceeds the column width. 'wrap' lets text wrap and the row grow taller; 'truncate' clips with an ellipsis (default-rendered cells show a tooltip on hover when truncated). Header cells always truncate.

props.name: plugins
props.description: Named plugins that extend table behavior via the transform pipeline. Converted to an ordered array internally.

props.name: rowIndexStart
props.description: ARIA row index (1-based) for the first rendered body row. The row ordinal is an accessibility concern independent of any visible index column, so setting this (or rowCount) makes the table emit aria-rowindex on body rows and aria-rowcount on the table. For a paginated/windowed view, pass the offset of the first visible row (e.g. (page - 1) * pageSize + 1) so aria-rowindex reflects position in the full dataset. Data-driven mode only.

props.name: rowCount
props.description: Total number of body rows across all pages/windows, used for aria-rowcount so assistive tech can announce "row X of Y" against the full dataset. When omitted but rowIndexStart is set (windowed view with an unknown total), aria-rowcount is set to -1 per the ARIA unknown-count convention. Data-driven mode only.

props.name: children
props.description: Children mode: compose the table yourself from TableHeader / TableBody / TableFooter, each holding TableRow and TableCell, instead of using data-driven rendering. The children are passed straight to the <table>, so the section is yours to supply. A TableRow placed directly in Table emits <table><tr>, which is invalid HTML and mismatches on hydration (the parser inserts an implied <tbody> for server-rendered markup; React does not on the client). Data-driven mode renders the sections for you.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

components.name: TableBody
components.description: <tbody> wrapper for children mode. Holds the data rows. A row must sit inside a section: <table> cannot contain a <tr> directly, because the HTML parser inserts an implied <tbody> when it parses server-rendered markup and React does not when it renders on the client, so rows written straight into Table mismatch on hydration. The data-driven data={...} mode renders this element itself; in children mode it is yours to supply.

props.name: children
props.description: The <tbody> rows.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization. Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

components.name: TableCell
components.description: <td> wrapper that reads TableContext to apply density padding, font size, and divider borders when used inside Table.

props.name: children
props.description: Cell content.

components.name: TableFooter
components.description: <tfoot> wrapper for children mode. Holds summary or total rows beneath the body. A row must sit inside a section: <table> cannot contain a <tr> directly, because the HTML parser inserts an implied <tbody> when it parses server-rendered markup and React does not when it renders on the client, so the two trees mismatch on hydration. Children mode only: the data-driven data={...} path renders a header and a body, never a footer.

props.name: children
props.description: The <tfoot> rows.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization. Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

components.name: TableHeader
components.description: <thead> wrapper for children mode. Holds the header row, whose cells are TableHeaderCell. A row must sit inside a section: <table> cannot contain a <tr> directly, because the HTML parser inserts an implied <tbody> when it parses server-rendered markup and React does not when it renders on the client, so the two trees mismatch on hydration. The data-driven data={...} mode renders this element itself whenever columns are supplied; in children mode it is yours to supply.

props.name: children
props.description: The <thead> rows.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization. Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

components.name: TableHeaderCell
components.description: <th> wrapper that reads TableContext to apply density padding, semibold weight, secondary text color, and divider borders when used inside Table.

props.name: children
props.description: Header cell content.

components.name: TableRow
components.description: <tr> wrapper that reads TableContext to apply striped, hover, and divider styles when used inside Table.

props.name: children
props.description: Row cell elements.

components.name: TableSelectionToolbar
components.description: Selection-aware bulk-action surface built on Toolbar. Pass selectionState from useTableSelectionState so count, visibility, and complete clearing stay synchronized with the Table selection plugin. The component owns no table or sticky layout: place it in flow or apply caller-owned positioning through xstyle.

props.name: selection
props.description: Shared selection state returned by useTableSelectionState: selectedKeys, selectedCount, hasSelection, and clearSelection.

props.name: startContent
props.description: Product-owned action controls aligned to the logical start. Child controls inherit the toolbar size.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name for the action surface.

props.name: renderSelectionLabel
props.description: Overrides the visible count text for localisation or domain-specific copy.

props.name: clearLabel
props.description: Visible label for the command that clears the complete controlled selection.

props.name: size
props.description: Toolbar size. Cascades to product action controls and the clear action.

props.name: variant
props.description: Toolbar surface variant.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: Caller-owned layout styles, including sticky positioning for floating compositions.

components.name: TabList
components.description: Tab strip that provides TabListContext (value, onChange, size) to Tab and TabMenu children; a nav landmark, or the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern where role="tablist" asks for it.

props.name: value
props.description: The currently selected tab value.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Callback fired when a tab is selected.

props.name: size
props.description: Size variant applied to all child tabs.

props.name: layout
props.description: Layout mode for tab sizing. 'hug': each tab hugs its content width. 'fill': tabs stretch equally to fill the container width.

props.name: hasDivider
props.description: Whether to show a bottom border divider under the tab list.

props.name: isFullBleed
props.description: Makes the tab strip escape its parent's container padding, extending to the container's content edges (cancels the nearest padded Layout container's --container-padding-* custom properties with negative margins). The inner strip pads back by the portion of the container inset that is not already supplied by the first or last tab stop, keeping edge labels aligned while a hasDivider underline spans the full content width. Matches Divider's isFullBleed: inline (start/end) edges only; block-edge docking stays with the surrounding layout.

props.name: role
props.description: ARIA role for the strip. 'tablist' asks for the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern: role="tablist" / role="tab" and aria-selected, with each tab pointing at the panel it controls via its panelId; only tabs may live in a tablist strip, and an href on a tab is ignored there. Left unset, the strip is a nav landmark marking the current tab with aria-current. Any other value is passed through to the element unchanged.

props.name: overflow
props.description: What happens when the tabs are wider than the strip. 'auto' lets the component choose, which today always scrolls. 'scroll' scrolls the tabs horizontally, with edge fades and arrow affordances for pointers that can hover. 'visible' turns overflow handling off and lets the tabs spill out of the strip. The selected tab is always scrolled back into view.

props.name: children
props.description: Tab and TabMenu items to render inside the strip.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

components.name: TabMenu
components.description: Overflow menu trigger that opens a dropdown of additional tab options, showing the selected option's label as the trigger text. Host attributes and DOM event handlers (id, aria-*, data-*, drag and drop) reach the trigger button, not the popup or its options. The button keeps its role, tab stop, and menu disclosure attributes.

props.name: label
props.description: Label for the trigger button (shown when no option is selected) and the dropdown heading divider.

props.name: options
props.description: Array of menu options rendered in the dropdown.

components.name: Text
components.description: Semantic body text component that renders text with type-based styling from the theme, with optional truncation, decoration, and layout props.

props.name: type
props.description: Semantic text type. Determines size, weight, and line-height from the theme. 'inherit' takes all three from the surrounding text instead. Themes may add custom types. Note: this prop is called `type`, not `variant`.

props.name: children
props.description: Text content.

props.name: size
props.description: Explicit font size override. Overrides the size from `type` but preserves other type properties. Prefer using `type` alone.

props.name: color
props.description: Text color. Defaults to 'secondary' for the 'supporting' type, 'primary' for all others. Themes may add custom colors.

props.name: weight
props.description: Font weight override.

props.name: display
props.description: Display type. Silently overridden to 'block' when maxLines > 0 or hasCapsize is true.

props.name: as
props.description: HTML element to render.

props.name: maxLines
props.description: Maximum lines before truncation. 0 means no truncation. When set, shows a tooltip on hover if content is truncated.

props.name: hasTruncateTooltip
props.description: Controls tooltip behavior for truncated text. true shows the tooltip at the default position, false disables it, or a placement string ('above' | 'below' | 'start' | 'end') sets a specific position.

props.name: wordBreak
props.description: Word break behavior when truncating. Defaults to 'break-all' for single-line truncation, 'break-word' otherwise. Without truncation, a token longer than its line (a URL, an ID) wraps (`overflow-wrap: break-word`), so in ordinary flow text does not make the page scroll sideways. Inside a flex row, give the flex child `min-width: 0` so it can shrink. A container you style with `overflow-wrap: anywhere` does not reach this text; Astryx's own containers pass their wrap through.

props.name: textWrap
props.description: Text wrapping behavior.

props.name: justify
props.description: Text alignment (justification). Uses logical values (start/end) for i18n/RTL compatibility.

props.name: hasCapsize
props.description: Enable optical alignment using text-box-trim. Forces block display.

props.name: hasStrikethrough
props.description: Apply strikethrough text decoration.

props.name: hasTabularNumbers
props.description: Use tabular (monospace) numbers for aligned numeric data.

props.name: id
props.description: HTML id attribute.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

components.name: TextArea
components.description: TextArea is a multi-line text input for collecting longer-form content like comments, descriptions, or messages. Use it when the expected input spans multiple lines. For shorter, single-line values, use TextInput.

props.name: ref
props.description: Ref forwarded to the underlying <textarea> element.

props.name: label
props.description: Label text for the textarea. Always rendered for accessibility.

props.name: value
props.description: Current value of the textarea.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Callback fired when the textarea value changes.

props.name: changeAction
props.description: Async action fired after onChange inside a React transition. Enables optimistic updates via useOptimistic.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Visually hides the label while keeping it accessible to screen readers.

props.name: description
props.description: Helper text displayed between the label and textarea.

props.name: isOptional
props.description: Displays an "Optional" indicator next to the label. Mutually exclusive with isRequired.

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Displays a "Required" indicator next to the label and sets aria-required. Mutually exclusive with isOptional.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables the textarea, preventing interaction.

props.name: isReadOnly
props.description: Makes the textarea read-only: the value is shown at full opacity and still submits with the form, but cannot be edited. Unlike isDisabled, a read-only textarea is not dimmed and keeps its form value. isDisabled takes precedence when both are set.

props.name: disabledMessage
props.description: Explains why the textarea is disabled. With isDisabled, shows a tooltip on hover/keyboard focus and keeps the textarea focusable via aria-disabled (the field becomes read-only). Use this instead of wrapping a disabled TextArea in Tooltip, so the reason is attached to the field itself.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Puts the textarea in a loading state, showing a spinner inside the input.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder text shown when the textarea is empty.

props.name: rows
props.description: Number of visible text rows.

props.name: maxLength
props.description: Maximum number of characters allowed, counted as user-perceived characters: an emoji or flag sequence counts as one. When set, a character counter (current/max) is displayed inside the input container, anchored to the bottom-right beneath the text. Does not enforce the limit natively; when exceeded the counter turns red and shows a warning icon (a non-color cue), and screen-reader users hear the remaining/over-limit count announced. Consumers validating the limit should count with characterCount (exported from the package) so enforcement matches the displayed count.

props.name: status
props.description: Status indicator that applies a colored border and icon. An optional message is displayed in a floating box below the textarea.

props.name: statusVariant
props.description: How the status message is placed relative to the input. attached overlaps directly below the input (bordered treatment); detached floats below as a separate element with spacing; tooltip hides the message box and surfaces it in a tooltip on the status icon.

props.name: labelTooltip
props.description: Tooltip text displayed in an info icon at the end of the label.

props.name: startIcon
props.description: Icon component rendered inside the leading edge of the textarea wrapper. See `astryx docs icons` for valid semantic names.

props.name: hasSpellCheck
props.description: Enables or disables browser spell checking.

props.name: hasAutoFocus
props.description: Automatically focuses the textarea on mount.

props.name: size
props.description: Size of the textarea, affecting internal padding. Height is controlled by rows, not size.

props.name: onPaste
props.description: Callback fired when content is pasted into the textarea.

props.name: htmlName
props.description: HTML name attribute for the textarea element, useful for form submissions.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the field (number = pixels, string used as-is, e.g. "100%"). Sizes the whole field (label, control, and status) so they stay aligned.

props.name: onFocus
props.description: Callback fired when the textarea receives focus.

props.name: onBlur
props.description: Callback fired when the textarea loses focus.

props.name: autoComplete
props.description: The native autocomplete attribute, forwarded to the textarea unchanged. Does not affect the controlled value.

props.name: enterKeyHint
props.description: What the Return key of a touch keyboard says (the native `enterkeyhint`). iOS gives `done`, `go`, `next`, `search` and `send` their own key (a glyph on iOS 26: a checkmark, an arrow, a chevron, a magnifier, an up arrow); `enter` and `previous` keep the plain Return key. Chrome on Android (Gboard) gives every value its own key; with no hint a TextArea keeps Return. It only labels the key: what Enter does stays with your handlers.

props.name: inputMode
props.description: Which touch keyboard the field asks for (the native `inputmode`) without changing what it accepts: `numeric` brings up the number pad, `decimal` the decimal pad, `tel` the phone pad, `search` the web-search keyboard (whose Return key reads Go on iOS even with `enterKeyHint="search"`).

props.name: autoCapitalize
props.description: When a touch keyboard capitalizes as you type (the native `autocapitalize`). Unset, iOS capitalizes sentences. `off` and `none` never capitalize; `on` and `sentences` capitalize each sentence.

props.name: hasAutoCorrect
props.description: Whether a touch keyboard corrects words as you type (the native `autocorrect`). Unset, the browser decides; turn it off for usernames, codes and other values that are not words.

props.name: containerXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the field container (label, control, and status together). No effect inside InputGroup (style the InputGroup instead) or in a `horizontal-labels` FormLayout. Root `xstyle`, `className`, and `style` are not accepted.

props.name: containerClassName
props.description: Class name for the field container. Same targeting as `containerXstyle`.

props.name: containerStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the field container. Same targeting as `containerXstyle`.

props.name: controlXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the visual control box: the element that paints the border and background and holds icons and end controls. Never the native input.

props.name: controlClassName
props.description: Class name for the visual control box.

props.name: controlStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the visual control box.

components.name: TextInput
components.description: TextInput collects short-form text like names, emails, or search queries. Use it for single-line values where the expected input is brief. Pair it with validation status to guide users through required or formatted fields.

props.name: type
props.description: The HTML input type. `email`, `tel` and `url` also bring up the matching touch keyboard (email, phone pad, URL); `search` makes the field a search box (pair it with `enterKeyHint="search"` for a Search key on iOS; Chrome on Android shows one for `type="search"` alone).

props.name: label
props.description: Label text for the input: always rendered for accessibility.

props.name: value
props.description: Current value of the input.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Callback fired when the input value changes.

props.name: changeAction
props.description: Async action fired after onChange (if not prevented). Triggers optimistic update and shows a loading spinner while pending.

props.name: size
props.description: Size variant of the input.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Visually hides the label while keeping it accessible to screen readers.

props.name: description
props.description: Description text displayed between the label and input.

props.name: isOptional
props.description: Displays an "Optional" indicator next to the label. Mutually exclusive with isRequired.

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Displays a "Required" indicator next to the label and sets aria-required. Mutually exclusive with isOptional.

props.name: onEnter
props.description: Callback fired when the user presses the Enter key. IME-safe: Enter used to commit a Japanese/Chinese/Korean conversion does not fire it.

props.name: onKeyDown
props.description: Callback fired on keydown events on the input.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables the input, preventing interaction and dimming the element.

props.name: isReadOnly
props.description: Makes the input read-only: the value is shown at full opacity and still submits with the form, but cannot be edited. Unlike isDisabled, a read-only input is not dimmed and keeps its form value. isDisabled takes precedence when both are set.

props.name: disabledMessage
props.description: Explains why the input is disabled. With isDisabled, shows a tooltip on hover/keyboard focus and keeps the input focusable via aria-disabled (the field becomes read-only). Use this instead of wrapping a disabled TextInput in Tooltip, so the reason is attached to the field itself.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Puts the input in a loading state, showing a spinner and setting aria-busy.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder text shown when the input is empty.

props.name: labelTooltip
props.description: Tooltip text displayed in an info icon at the end of the label.

props.name: startIcon
props.description: SVG icon component displayed at the start of the input. See `astryx docs icons` for valid semantic names.

props.name: status
props.description: Validation status: applies a colored border and status icon. If message is provided, displays a floating message below the input. Error type also sets aria-invalid.

props.name: statusVariant
props.description: How the status message is placed relative to the input. attached overlaps directly below the input (bordered treatment); detached floats below as a separate element with spacing; tooltip hides the message box and surfaces it in a tooltip on the status icon.

props.name: hasClear
props.description: Shows a clear (×) button when the input has a value. Clicking it clears the value and returns focus to the input.

props.name: hasAutoFocus
props.description: Automatically focuses the input on mount.

props.name: htmlName
props.description: The HTML name attribute for the input, useful for form submissions.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the field (number = pixels, string used as-is, e.g. "100%"). Sizes the whole field (label, control, and status) so they stay aligned. Without a width the field can shrink with its row, so a filter bar never overflows; use `<HStack wrap="wrap">` when the controls should move to a second line instead.

props.name: autoComplete
props.description: The native autocomplete attribute, forwarded to the input unchanged. Does not affect the controlled value. It is also how AutoFill knows what a field holds: tag sign-in, address and payment fields (`username`, `new-password`, `one-time-code`, `email`, `tel`, `street-address`, …).

props.name: enterKeyHint
props.description: What the Return key of a touch keyboard says (the native `enterkeyhint`). iOS gives `done`, `go`, `next`, `search` and `send` their own key (a glyph on iOS 26: a checkmark, an arrow, a chevron, a magnifier, an up arrow); `enter` and `previous` keep the plain Return key. Chrome on Android (Gboard) gives every value its own key, `enter` and `previous` included; with no hint the key reads Next while another field follows, and a `type="url"` field shows Next instead of `go` while another field follows. It only labels the key: what Enter does stays with your handlers.

props.name: inputMode
props.description: Which touch keyboard the field asks for (the native `inputmode`) without changing what it accepts: `numeric` brings up the number pad, `decimal` the decimal pad, `tel` the phone pad, `search` the web-search keyboard (whose Return key reads Go on iOS even with `enterKeyHint="search"`; Chrome on Android shows the Enter key for `inputMode="search"` alone).

props.name: autoCapitalize
props.description: When a touch keyboard capitalizes as you type (the native `autocapitalize`). Unset, iOS capitalizes sentences, except in a URL field. `off` and `none` never capitalize; `on` and `sentences` capitalize each sentence.

props.name: hasAutoCorrect
props.description: Whether a touch keyboard corrects words as you type (the native `autocorrect`). Unset, the browser decides; turn it off for usernames, codes and other values that are not words.

props.name: hasSpellCheck
props.description: Whether misspelled words are underlined (the native `spellcheck`). Unset, the browser decides.

props.name: containerXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the field container (label, control, and status together). No effect inside InputGroup (style the InputGroup instead) or in a `horizontal-labels` FormLayout. Root `xstyle`, `className`, and `style` are not accepted.

props.name: containerClassName
props.description: Class name for the field container. Same targeting as `containerXstyle`.

props.name: containerStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the field container. Same targeting as `containerXstyle`.

props.name: controlXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the visual control box: the element that paints the border and background and holds icons and end controls. Never the native input.

props.name: controlClassName
props.description: Class name for the visual control box.

props.name: controlStyle
props.description: Inline styles for the visual control box.

components.name: Theme

props.name: theme
props.description: Theme object to apply. Prefer built theme objects for static production themes; use runtime `defineTheme()` for dynamic themes. Its `motion` can set `tempo` (0.75–1.5) and `character` (`'crisp' | 'standard' | 'expressive'`).

props.name: mode
props.description: Color mode. System follows OS preference.

props.name: children
props.description: Content to render with the theme.

components.name: Thumbnail
components.description: Thumbnail displays a compact, square preview of an image attachment. It shows a shimmer effect while uploading, the image on success, and a placeholder icon when no source is set. Use it in chat composers, file upload lists, or anywhere you need a small image preview with optional remove and click actions.

props.name: src
props.description: Image source URL.

props.name: alt
props.description: Alt text for the image. When omitted, the image is explicitly decorative (alt="", role="presentation", aria-hidden) and hidden from screen readers; a dev warning fires if neither alt nor label is set.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label (e.g. file name). Shown as tooltip on hover.

props.name: onRemove
props.description: Callback for the overlaid remove button.

props.name: onClick
props.description: Click handler. Adds button semantics and a hover overlay.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Shows skeleton (no src) or upload overlay (with src).

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether the thumbnail is disabled.

props.name: showRemoveOn
props.description: When the remove button is visible. `hover` (the default) reveals it on hover and on keyboard focus, and keeps it visible on any touch-capable device; `always` shows it at rest. Only applies when `onRemove` is set.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

props.name: className
props.description: CSS class name for the root element. Prefer xstyle for styling; className is provided for integration with non-StyleX systems.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles for the root element. Prefer xstyle for styling; inline styles bypass StyleX optimization.

props.name: data-testid
props.description: Test selector for automated testing frameworks.

components.name: TimeInput
components.description: TimeInput uses a browser/OS time picker on coarse pointers by default and Astryx's typed field on fine pointers. It converts values to a standard format and supports arrow-key adjustment on the typed surface. Use it in forms, scheduling flows, or any interface where users need to select a specific time.

props.name: label
props.description: Label text for the input (required for accessibility).

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Visually hides the label while keeping it accessible to screen readers.

props.name: description
props.description: Description text displayed between the label and input.

props.name: isOptional
props.description: Shows an "(optional)" indicator next to the label. Mutually exclusive with isRequired.

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Marks the field as required and sets aria-required. Mutually exclusive with isOptional.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables the input and suppresses interactions. The input stays focusable and exposes `aria-disabled`.

props.name: disabledMessage
props.description: Explains why the input is disabled. With isDisabled, shows a tooltip on hover/keyboard focus and describes the input (activation stays blocked). Use this instead of wrapping a disabled TimeInput in Tooltip.

props.name: value
props.description: Controlled time value in ISO format (HH:MM or HH:MM:SS).

props.name: onChange
props.description: Callback fired when the time changes. Receives undefined when the input is cleared.

props.name: changeAction
props.description: Async action fired after onChange. Wrapped in a React transition to provide optimistic UI; triggers the loading spinner while pending.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Puts the input into a loading state, displaying a spinner.

props.name: min
props.description: Minimum selectable time in ISO format. Values outside the range are rejected.

props.name: max
props.description: Maximum selectable time in ISO format. Values outside the range are rejected.

props.name: hasSeconds
props.description: Includes seconds in the time display and parsing.

props.name: hasClear
props.description: Shows a clear button when a value is set and the input is not disabled.

props.name: hourFormat
props.description: Controls the display format. '12h' shows the locale's day period (e.g. '2:30 PM', '오후 2:30'); '24h' uses 24-hour notation (e.g. '14:30'). When unset, follows the InternationalizationProvider locale's hour cycle: en-US reads 12-hour, en-GB and de-DE read 24-hour. To honor a person's own preference, pass it on the locale tag (e.g. 'en-US-u-hc-h23') rather than per field.

props.name: increment
props.description: Number of minutes to add or subtract when the user presses the up or down arrow key. Steps are whole minutes; a fractional value leaves the time unchanged.

props.name: presentation
props.description: Which surface selects the time. 'adaptive-native' (the default) uses Astryx's typed field on a fine pointer and the browser/OS input type=time on a coarse pointer — except hasSeconds or increment other than 1, which retain the typed field because iOS has no seconds wheel and treats step as validation rather than picker cadence; 'native' always uses the browser/OS control with no Astryx fallback; 'adaptive-bottom-sheet' uses the typed field on a fine pointer and Astryx's bottom-sheet time wheels on a coarse pointer; 'bottom-sheet' forces the wheels on every pointer; 'text-input' (like 'popover', which has no distinct TimeInput surface) keeps only the typed field. Native mode forwards min/max and enforces them on commit. hourFormat formats the closed value; the open OS picker follows the device locale.

props.name: nativePicker
props.description: Deprecated: use presentation ('touch' = 'adaptive-native', 'always' = 'native', 'never' = 'text-input'). Still works exactly as released; presentation wins when both are set.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder text shown when no time is selected. When the input is focused and empty, a format hint overrides this text.

props.name: size
props.description: Controls the height of the input element.

props.name: status
props.description: Status indicator that colors the border and displays an icon. When a message is provided it is rendered below the input.

props.name: statusVariant
props.description: How the status message is placed relative to the input. attached overlaps directly below the input (bordered treatment); detached floats below as a separate element with spacing; tooltip hides the message box and surfaces it in a tooltip on the status icon.

props.name: labelTooltip
props.description: Tooltip text rendered as an info icon at the end of the label row.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the field (number = pixels, string used as-is, e.g. "100%"). Sizes the whole field (label, control, and status) so they stay aligned.

props.name: containerXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the Field box around the label, control, and status. containerClassName and containerStyle take a class name and inline styles for the same box. No effect (development warning) where no Field box renders: inside InputGroup (style the group) and in a horizontal-labels FormLayout.

props.name: controlXstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the visual control box: the bordered element that holds the text, icons, and end controls, never the native input. controlClassName and controlStyle take a class name and inline styles for the same box. Replaces root xstyle, className, and style, which this component does not accept.

components.name: Timer
components.description: Displays a standardized elapsed duration for active work without scheduling a React render on every tick. Elapsed format updates by second below one hour and by minute after one hour; clock format remains second-precise.

props.name: startTime
props.description: Unix time in milliseconds when the measured operation began. Omit it to start from this Timer's mount.

props.name: format
props.description: Standard duration representation. Elapsed uses compact units and drops seconds after one hour; clock uses m:ss or h:mm:ss.

props.name: type
props.description: Semantic text type. Uses the same typography behavior as Timestamp.

props.name: size
props.description: Explicit font size override. Overrides the size from type.

props.name: color
props.description: Text color.

props.name: weight
props.description: Font weight override.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for the Text wrapper. Must be a stylex.create() value.

props.name: className
props.description: CSS class name for the Text wrapper. Prefer xstyle for styling.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline styles for the Text wrapper. Prefer xstyle for styling.

components.name: Timestamp
components.description: Timestamp formats a date or time value into human-readable text. Use it to show when something was created, updated, or is scheduled; picking relative for recency, absolute for precision, or auto to let the component decide.

props.name: value
props.description: The date/time to display. Accepts Unix timestamps (seconds) or ISO 8601 strings.

props.name: format
props.description: Display format. 'relative' uses the locale's native long relative-time wording ('2 hours ago' in English), 'relative_short' uses its narrow pattern ('2h ago' in English) for compact surfaces, 'date' shows 'Mar 21, 2025', 'date_long' shows 'March 21, 2025', 'date_weekday' shows 'Wed, Mar 21, 2025', 'date_time' shows 'Mar 21, 2025, 2:51 PM', 'time' shows '2:51 PM', 'system_*' variants use ISO-style formatting, 'unix_seconds' shows the Unix time in whole seconds since the epoch (an absolute, zone-independent value), 'auto' switches from relative to date_time based on recency. Absolute formats never read the current time. 'relative', 'relative_short' and 'auto' read it on the client only: a server render or static prerender shows the full date and time in UTC, labelled, and the client switches to the format's normal output after hydration. Date-bearing formats ('date', 'date_long', 'date_weekday', 'date_time', and the full date in the hover card and the accessible name) use the InternationalizationProvider calendar, such as calendar="persian"; 'time', the relative formats, 'system_*', and 'unix_seconds' do not change.

props.name: autoThreshold
props.description: Threshold in seconds for 'auto' format to switch from relative to date_time.

props.name: hasTooltip
props.description: Whether to show a copyable hover card with the full date/time on hover. Applies to relative timestamps and to any format once tooltipEntries is configured.

props.name: tooltipEntries
props.type: ReadonlyArray<{timezoneID?: string; format?: TimestampTooltipFormat; label?: string; isCopyable?: boolean}>
props.description: Lines to show on hover, so one instant can be read (and optionally copied) in several time zones and/or formats at once. Each entry is one line, in the order given. Omit timezoneID (or pass 'local') for the viewer's own zone; format defaults to the full absolute style and also accepts 'full' alongside every non-relative TimestampFormat. Rows are read-only unless they set isCopyable (default false); copyable rows show a copy button in a dedicated trailing action column so buttons align, and the column is only present when some row is copyable. With no entries the card shows a single default row with the full absolute time, which is copyable. Configuring entries also attaches the surface to absolute formats, which otherwise have none.

props.name: isTimezoneShown
props.description: Whether to append the timezone abbreviation to the visible text. Applies to the date_time and time formats; system_* formats stay machine-readable and never carry one. Use tooltipEntries to control the tooltip's time zones.

props.name: isLive
props.description: Whether the relative time should update live (e.g. "2 min ago" → "3 min ago").

props.name: type
props.description: Semantic text type from Text. Determines size, weight, and line-height.

props.name: size
props.description: Explicit font size override. Overrides the size from type.

props.name: color
props.description: Text color.

props.name: weight
props.description: Font weight override.

components.name: Toast
components.description:
Toast shows a brief, non-blocking notification to confirm an action or present temporary information. Use it for scenarios where the user needs feedback but not a decision, such as saving, deleting, or changing a status.

For production use, prefer the `useToast()` hook; it handles positioning, stacking, auto-dismiss, and deduplication via `ToastViewport`. Toasts stay within viewport and safe-area gutters, wrap long message content, and enter, exit, or swipe-dismiss toward their configured top or bottom edge. The vertical swipe uses the same spatial model as placement motion: top Toasts leave upward and bottom Toasts leave downward. Swipe waits for dominant edge-directed intent before cancelling native touch movement and reports the existing manual dismissal reason. Pen is supported as direct-contact input; mouse drag is excluded to avoid conflicting with desktop text selection, where the visible close control remains available. Set `isAutoHide: false` explicitly when an action or message must remain available. The `Toast` component renders the visual toast element inline and is useful for previews, documentation, and static showcases where the viewport lifecycle is not needed.

props.name: body
props.description: Primary message content.

props.name: type
props.description: Toast type controlling background color. Error toasts persist until dismissed.

props.name: isAutoHide
props.description: Whether the toast auto-dismisses. Defaults to true for info, false for error.

props.name: autoHideDuration
props.description: Duration in ms before auto-dismiss. Timed content must satisfy WCAG 2.2.1.

props.name: endContent
props.description: Content rendered at the trailing end (e.g. Undo button, link). Keep action labels short.

props.name: uniqueID
props.description: Unique identifier for deduplication.

props.name: collisionBehavior
props.description: Behavior when a toast with matching uniqueID already exists.

props.name: onHide
props.description: Callback fired when the toast is removed.

props.name: onDismiss
props.description: Callback fired when the toast is dismissed.

props.name: renderContent
props.description: Replaces the content of this toast's card with your own layout. Astryx keeps the card, its astryx-toast theme target and auto-hide behavior (inside a ToastViewport the viewport announces the toast, and while a modal hosts the viewport the card announces itself), then hands the renderer the message, endContent, resolved toast settings and a dismiss callback. The custom renderer owns every control in its layout: compose the control you want and call dismiss from it. Astryx does not inject a fallback close into custom content. Per-toast: an app shares one layout by wrapping useToast and passing it on every call, while a toast raised by library code that never passes it renders as an ordinary Astryx toast. The argument is {body, endContent, type, isAutoHide, autoHideDuration, dismiss}, where type is 'info' | 'error'.

components.name: ToggleButton
components.description: A button that toggles between pressed and unpressed states. Thin wrapper over Button with controlled toggle pattern, icon swap, and font weight emphasis.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the button. Used as visible text, or as aria-label for icon-only buttons.

props.name: isPressed
props.description: Whether the button is currently pressed. Ignored for a ToggleButtonGroup member with a value.

props.name: onPressedChange
props.description: Called synchronously when pressed state should change. Receives the next state and the click event; call event.preventDefault() to skip pressedChangeAction. Without an Action, the callback produces no Action-pending feedback. Ignored for a ToggleButtonGroup member with a value.

props.name: pressedChangeAction
props.description: Action handler for API- or navigation-backed toggles, run in a transition after the synchronous onPressedChange callback unless that callback calls event.preventDefault(). Works without onPressedChange. Shows an optimistic pressed state and a spinner while pending, and remains interruptible by re-clicks. Omit it for callback-only toggles with no Action-pending feedback. Ignored for a ToggleButtonGroup member with a value.

props.name: size
props.description: Button size. Defaults to group size when inside a group.

props.name: elevation
props.description: Resting shadow depth for floating (FAB-style) toggle buttons, mirroring Button. `none` is the default flat button; `low`/`med`/`high` map to the shadow token scale. Applies inside a ToggleButtonGroup as well — grouped children retain their own elevation.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether the button is disabled.

props.name: isLoading
props.description: Whether the button shows a loading spinner.

props.name: icon
props.description: Icon element. When provided without children, button becomes icon-only with tooltip from label.

props.name: isIconOnly
props.description: When true, renders as a square icon-only button with `label` as the aria-label and an automatic tooltip from the label.

props.name: pressedIcon
props.description: Icon shown when pressed. Falls back to icon if not provided.

props.name: children
props.description: Visible content. If omitted with icon, button becomes icon-only.

props.name: tooltip
props.description: Tooltip text shown on hover.

props.name: value
props.description: Value identifier when used inside ToggleButtonGroup. Required in groups.

props.name: data-testid
props.description: Test selector for automated testing frameworks.

components.name: ToggleButtonGroup
components.description: Groups toggle buttons for exclusive (single) or multi-select behavior. Uses discriminated union on type for type-safe value/onChange.

props.name: children
props.description: ToggleButton children. Give each member a value; the group owns its pressed state and ignores its isPressed, onPressedChange, and pressedChangeAction props. Member activation calls the group’s onChange without starting a member Action transition.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the group (aria-label).

props.name: type
props.description: Selection mode. Single allows one active button, multiple allows many.

props.name: value
props.description: Currently selected value(s). Type depends on selection mode.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called when selection changes.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Layout direction of the button group.

props.name: size
props.description: Default size for buttons in the group. Individual buttons can override.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether all buttons in the group are disabled.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value.

props.name: data-testid
props.description: Test selector for automated testing frameworks.

components.name: Token
components.description: Token is a small, inline element for representing discrete pieces of associated data, like tags, categories, or selections. Use it to label content, show active filters, or represent removable items like selected recipients in a compose field.

props.name: label
props.description: Text label displayed inside the token.

props.name: size
props.description: The size of the token.

props.name: color
props.description: Color variant of the token.

props.name: icon
props.description: Optional icon rendered before the label.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether the token is disabled; reduces opacity and blocks interactions.

props.name: onRemove
props.description: Callback fired when the remove button is clicked. When provided, an X button is rendered inside the token.

props.name: onClick
props.description: Click handler. When provided, the token renders as a <span> container with an invisible <button> inside for accessibility.

props.name: href
props.description: Link URL. When provided, the token renders as an <a> element. The destination follows the shared navigation rule described on the Link `href` prop.

props.name: description
props.description: Accessible description applied via aria-description on the root element.

props.name: endContent
props.description: Content rendered after the label and before the remove button.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Visually hides the label using a screen-reader-only clip technique; the label remains accessible.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value, not an inline style object like style={{}}.

components.name: Tokenizer
components.description: Tokenizer is a multi-select input that lets users search, select, and manage multiple items displayed as removable chips. Use it when users need to build a set of selections from a searchable data source, like adding team members, applying tags, or choosing filters.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the input.

props.name: searchSource
props.description: Data source providing search and bootstrap methods. `search(query, context)` may call `context.update(items)` to show matches it already has before it returns; the value it returns is the final list, and every list after the first for a query keeps the shown rows first and adds new rows after them.

props.name: value
props.description: Array of currently selected items.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called when selection changes. The change argument includes the affected item and type ('add' | 'create' | 'remove' | 'reorder'). Additions and removals (including Backspace on an empty input) are announced to screen readers via a polite live region.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Input placeholder text. Only shown when no tokens are selected.

props.name: maxEntries
props.description: Maximum number of selections allowed. Input is hidden when the limit is reached.

props.name: hasClear
props.description: Show a clear-all button for bulk removal of all tokens.

props.name: renderToken
props.description: Custom render function for selected tokens. Default renders Token with label and onRemove.

props.name: renderItem
props.description: Custom render function for dropdown items. Default renders TypeaheadItem.

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Disables the input and all token interactions. The input keeps its tab stop: it is announced as disabled (aria-disabled), is read-only, and opens and picks nothing. With tokenOverflowBehavior="unfocusedLayer" and no disabledMessage, the input is natively disabled and out of the tab order.

props.name: htmlName
props.description: The HTML name attribute for form submissions. Renders one hidden input per selected item id.

props.name: disabledMessage
props.description: Explains why the tokenizer is disabled. With isDisabled, shows a tooltip on hover/keyboard focus and keeps the input focusable via aria-disabled (input stays blocked). Use this instead of wrapping a disabled Tokenizer in Tooltip, so the reason is attached to the field itself.

props.name: status
props.description: Validation status object with type and message for error/warning/success states.

props.name: statusVariant
props.description: How the status message is placed relative to the input. attached overlaps directly below the input (bordered treatment); detached floats below as a separate element with spacing; tooltip reveals the message in an info-tip button.

props.name: isLabelHidden
props.description: Visually hides the label while keeping it accessible.

props.name: description
props.description: Helper text displayed below the label.

props.name: isRequired
props.description: Marks the field as required.

props.name: isOptional
props.description: Shows an optional indicator on the label.

props.name: labelTooltip
props.description: Tooltip text shown on the label.

props.name: hasEntriesOnFocus
props.description: Show bootstrap results on focus before typing.

props.name: maxMenuItems
props.description: Maximum number of search results to display. The hasCreate entry is offered on top of them, so a menu can show one more than this.

props.name: menuWidth
props.description: Fixed dropdown width in pixels. The menu never shrinks below its anchor width.

props.name: minQueryLength
props.description: Minimum query length before the search source is queried. Below it no search runs, and the menu stays closed — unless hasCreate is set, in which case the "Create ..." entry is still offered, being derived from the typed text rather than fetched for it.

props.name: emptySearchText
props.description: Content shown when the query matched nothing. Takes a ReactNode, so the dead end can carry a link or a create row. Announced in a polite live region as the text it renders, read from the DOM; aria-hidden parts stay out of both, and content that renders no text announces nothing. null counts as not given, like undefined, and falls through to the default; pass an empty string to render nothing.

props.name: hasAutoFocus
props.description: Auto-focus the input on mount.

props.name: size
props.description: Input and token size.

props.name: debounceMs
props.description: Debounce delay in ms before triggering search. Set to 0 for synchronous sources, and for a source that shows local matches through `context.update` and delays its own server request.

props.name: hasCreate
props.description: Allow users to create new tokens from free-text input. When true, a "Create" option appears in the dropdown for typed text that doesn't match existing results. The onChange change type is 'create' for these items.

props.name: onChangeQuery
props.description: Callback fired when the search query text changes.

props.name: startIcon
props.description: Icon to display at the start of the input, before any tokens. Accepts a semantic icon name, an SVG icon component, or a ReactNode directly.

props.name: endContent
props.description: Content to display at the end of the input row. Useful for buttons, result counts, or other controls.

props.name: handleRef
props.description: Imperative handle exposing focusInput(), focusFirstToken(), focusLastToken(), clearInput(), and selectAll().

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the field (number = pixels, string used as-is, e.g. "100%"). Sizes the whole field (label, control, and status) so they stay aligned.

props.name: tokenOverflowBehavior
props.description: Controls how tokens overflow when the container is too narrow.

props.name: onFocus

props.name: presentation
props.description: How the field presents its choices. adaptive (the default) uses the bottom sheet on compact touch screens and the popover otherwise, resolved the same way Selector resolves it; the server render and the hydrating render are the popover. popover is the inline combobox with its anchored suggestion menu on every device. bottom-sheet replaces it on every device with a field showing the selected tokens, whose trigger opens one tall modal sheet: a search row on top, full-width checkbox rows that keep their place while the sheet is open, a Create row with hasCreate, and a footer pinned in every state with a confirmed Clear all and Save; the sheet edits a draft, so onChange fires once, when Save commits it, and a swipe, scrim or Escape close of a changed draft asks before discarding. In the sheet presentation the field box holds the trigger, the tokens and endContent, and keeps the box, theming target and focus ring of the inline field; the trigger is the control: ref, id, aria-* and data-* reach it, and ref receives the trigger button there, so type it Ref<HTMLInputElement | HTMLButtonElement>, which the component accepts (TokenizerProps keeps its released input ref type). endContent sits at the inline end of the field and renderToken renders its tokens, as in the inline field; their own controls act without opening the sheet. renderItem, hasClear (the sheet has its own Clear all), hasEntriesOnFocus, menuWidth, tokenOverflowBehavior (the field wraps its tokens) and hasAutoFocus have no surface in the sheet, and the field warns once in development when they are passed. components.name: useTableGroupedRows
components.description: Hook that groups a flat data array into collapsible section rows. Each distinct groupBy value becomes a full-width section-header row with a chevron toggle, the group label, and a member count; collapsing hides that group's data rows while keeping the header visible. The disclosure state lives on the chevron button, not the native table row. Mirrors useTableTreeState: the consumer owns the collapsedGroups set and the hook returns {data, plugin, idKey}: pass them to Table as data, plugins, and idKey respectively. Grouping runs on the rows you hand it, so with pagination the order is filter, sort, slice, then group: sort by the group key first and the user's keys second, so a section's rows stay contiguous and each page appends to the bottom of the table instead of splicing rows in above the reader. A page that ends on a row count still cuts mid-section, and the heading then counts what has loaded rather than what exists: "6" quietly becoming "10". Where the full result set is in hand, carry the cut forward to the end of the section it lands in: every rendered section is then whole and its count is a total.

props.name: data
props.description: The flat data to group.

props.name: groupBy
props.description: Derive the group key for a row. Rows with the same key share a section.

props.name: collapsedGroups
props.description: Set of currently-collapsed group keys.

props.name: onToggleGroup
props.description: Called with a group key when its header is toggled.

props.name: renderGroupHeader
props.type: (groupKey: string, count: number, collapsed: boolean) => ReactNode
props.description: Custom renderer for a group header's content (right of the chevron). Defaults to `<groupKey> (<count>)`.

props.name: getRowKey
props.description: Stable key for a real row. Falls back to a positional key when omitted.

props.name: groupOrder

components.description: Hook that returns a TablePlugin which expands a full-width detail panel below a row, rendered by the consumer via renderExpanded(item). Adds a leading chevron column and a right-click "Expand/Collapse row" action; the consumer owns the expandedKeys set. The panel spans the row but starts its content at the first column, past the chevron, so detail lines up with the labels above it; the inset follows the table density. Use it for master-detail rows (order details, forms, charts, nested tables). For hierarchical data where child rows reuse the parent columns, use useTableTreeData + useTableTreeState instead.

props.name: expandedKeys
props.description: Set of currently-expanded row keys. Consumer-owned.

props.name: onToggle
props.description: Called with a row key when its expansion is toggled (chevron click or context-menu action).

props.name: getRowKey
props.description: Derive a stable unique key from a row item.

props.name: getRowLabel
props.description: Derive a human-readable row identity for the chevron accessible name. Astryx combines it with localized expand/collapse wording. Omit it, or return blank text, to keep the generic "Expand row" and "Collapse row" labels.

props.name: renderExpanded
props.description: Render the detail content shown in a full-width panel below the row when it is expanded. Receives the row item.

props.name: getIsItemExpandable
props.description: Control which rows are expandable. Non-expandable rows show no chevron, no context-menu action, and never render a panel. Defaults to all rows expandable.

props.name: panelVariant
props.description: Background behind the detail panel. 'transparent' (default) paints nothing: the panel is the row's continuation and takes whatever surface the table sits on, so a Card shows through and a striped table's zebra reads on unchanged. 'muted' washes it, marking it as commentary rather than another row of data — reach for it in a bare table with no card, dividers or striping, where nothing else makes that distinction. The wash is a low-alpha near-black, so it is close to invisible over a dark card: 'muted' is largely a light-theme effect.

props.name: hasRowClickExpansion
props.description: Toggle a row by clicking anywhere on it, not only on its chevron. A pointer-only convenience layered over the chevron, which stays the accessible control for keyboard and assistive tech. Clicks on interactive cell content (buttons, links, form controls) or on a text selection do not toggle, and non-expandable rows stay inert.

props.name: animatedLayout

With it, opening or closing a panel glides the rows after it (and the content after the table) to their new places instead of jumping, the opening panel plays in on the same motion, and each row's divider moves with it. Under Reduce Motion the rows fade in place on a touch screen and change at once with a mouse; in a table with column lines (dividers columns or grid, which do not move yet) they change at once. Without it, rows jump.

Numbering follows the rendered data order (reflecting the current sort / filter / pagination view) and starts at 1 by default. Astryx renderCell receives only the row item, so the plugin takes the rendered data array to derive each ordinal.

props.name: data
props.description: The data array currently rendered by the table (post sort/filter/page). Numbering follows this order.

props.name: getRowKey

props.name: label
props.description: Header label for the index column.

props.name: startFrom
props.description: First index value.

components.name: useTableRowStatus
components.description: Hook that returns a TablePlugin which prepends a narrow column signaling per-row status. Return {status, label} for a semantic success, warning, or error: Table resolves the matching glyph and tone through the active theme. Return {color, icon?, label} for a custom marker: every color is paint-only, an omitted icon renders the stable 8px dot, and an explicit icon renders that caller-selected glyph. Named custom icons keep their released Icon color mapping; raw CSS custom icons inherit the caller's exact paint instead of the previous primary fallback. Existing callers require no source migration. label is required and becomes the accessible image name plus supplemental hover tooltip; return null for no indicator. The column header is visually blank but carries a screen-reader-only localized name ("Row status", i18n key @astryx.table.rowStatus.columnHeader). Memoize getStatus with useCallback for a stable plugin identity.

props.name: getStatus
props.type: (item: T) => ({ status: 'success' | 'warning' | 'error'; color?: never; icon?: never; label: string } | { status?: never; color: 'accent' | 'success' | 'error' | 'warning' | 'red' | 'orange' | 'green' | 'yellow' | 'blue' | 'gray' | string; icon?: IconName; label: string }) | null
props.description: Derive either a semantic outcome or a custom marker. {status, label} accepts the closed success/error/warning vocabulary and resolves its glyph and tone through the active theme. {color, icon?, label} preserves the stable custom-marker path: color always selects paint, no icon renders an 8px dot, and icon renders the explicit caller glyph. Even color values named success/error/warning remain dots without icon. Valid icon names: close, chevronDown, chevronLeft, chevronRight, chevronsLeft, chevronsRight, check, success, error, warning, info, calendar, clock, externalLink, menu, moreHorizontal, search, upload, arrowUp, arrowDown, arrowsUpDown, funnel, eyeSlash, viewColumns, copy, checkDouble, wrench, stop, microphone. The branches are exclusive, label is required and announced via role="img", and null leaves the row status cell empty. Memoize with useCallback for a stable plugin identity.
